changes: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts: two behavioural changes against main. The POSIX absolute-path rule in normalizeGateReason (extracted as its own exported function) now matches only at a token start, so a slash-bearing identifier like DEV/REVIEW and a repo-relative path like src/core/alpha.ts are no longer rewritten to one token, while host-varying absolute paths still collapse. And gateFailureDigest's prefix is signals-conditional: when extractGateBlockSignals returns nothing, the prefix widens so a signal-less reason that diverges late keeps a distinct key. convergence-breaker-smoke.ts: a rebuilt case matrix with named cases and guard tags. packages/main/tests/red/: two committed, runnable test artifacts — a RED harness and a differential-vs-main probe.
usage: No user-facing command. The convergence breaker is internal: gateFailureDigest(command, reason) keys the per-story gate-failure counter. Run node packages/main/dist/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.js for the case matrix, and node packages/main/tests/red/red-s3-differential-probe.mjs <fresh-main-dist> to compare this build against main.
expectedOutcome: Two false-freeze classes that main mints one key for stop being conflated: a story whose gate rejection names DEV/REVIEW then DEV/TEST, or src/core/alpha.ts then src/core/beta.ts, now gets distinct keys and is not frozen as a repeat. A genuine repeat of the same failure, and every ambiguous bare identifier, still collapses so the brake still trips.
actualTranscript: convergence-breaker-smoke.js prints its must-differ cases at keys=2 counter=1 breaker=proceed and its must-still-collapse cases at keys=1 counter=2 breaker=trips, exit 0. The RED harness passes on this branch and fails against a freshly built main on exactly the delivered classes. The differential probe reports zero pairs where this build collapses what main distinguishes.
outcomeDiff: Delivered less than the original checklist asked. CHK-002 and CHK-004 landed in full. CHK-001 landed in the bounded form only: the primary C1 fix was delivered on main by sibling story B-cc54, which this branch adopts unchanged, and this story contributes the signals-conditional prefix. CHK-003 did not land and was proven undeliverable from message text alone, with an operator-confirmed scope shrinkage recorded; see limitations.
limitations: CHK-003 was withdrawn, not delivered, and the withdrawal is a proof rather than a shortfall of effort. Recognising a lifecycle artifact ordinal in a gate rejection requires telling it apart from a third-party test label of the same shape, and the two are the same string because test output is interpolated verbatim into the rejection at machine.ts:1190. Eight successive recognition rules were each broken by cross-host review on a different token shape before the eighth showed they were eight measurements of one impossibility; for a brake the tie breaks toward collapse because over-recognising lets a retry mint a fresh key forever. The operator confirmed the scope shrinkage and scope-shrinkage-decision.json lists CHK-003 as removed. The test suite asserts the opposite of what CHK-003 asked, so the withdrawal is machine-checked. One frozen artifact stays stale by a tooling limit that no phase after PLAN can correct: proofstory_contract_set is PLAN-only (command-policy.ts:420), so the AB-003 acceptance binding still reads as if ordinals stay distinct; this is recorded partially_mitigated and a workflow task was filed to add a withdrawn state. The follow-up that could achieve CHK-003 needs the digest to consult story state to know which ordinals exist, which makes it store-dependent on a hot path.
pitfalls: This ran 25+ review rounds and 62 cross-host findings; the code stabilised around round 20 and most later rounds were record-quality defects of the main agent, not code. Four recurring traps for the next person: (1) a boundary assertion for recognising ids leaks — it leaked eight times to eight punctuation shapes; the only closed form is a whole-token equality test with zero reduction, and even that cannot separate an id from an identically-shaped label. (2) Every time the case matrix changes, re-record ALL evidence notes as a whole set and cite case names and guard tags, never hand-written counts — a partial re-record leaves sibling notes contradicting each other, and counts go stale. (3) Do not re-run an evidence-producing command that already passes: after a git merge main that stales only the review passes, re-run the passes, not quorum_submit — quorum round ids omit the material digest, so a second submit double-writes and invalidates all rounds, with no supersede path; recovery needed surgically removing the duplicate events from the append-only, un-chained process-events.jsonl. (4) The quorum-submit-smoke validate budget was raised to 20m on main because the suite grew past its 600s budget and was deterministically failing every story's phase advance.
